options.misconception: By 2019 the flow had shifted toward Central American families, not single Mexican adults.
options.text: A rise in crossings by single adults from Mexico, as in 2000

rationales.A: Background: in 2019, families were 473,682 of the 851,508 apprehensions, more than half, and migrants from El Salvador, Guatemala, and Honduras made up 81 percent of all apprehensions. In 2000, single adults from Mexico dominated.
rationales.B: Background: tourists who overstay visas are counted at airports, not in Border Patrol apprehensions.
rationales.C: Background: the table covers the border with Mexico, where the 2019 arrivals came from Central America.
rationales.D: Background: single adults were only 301,806 of the 851,508 apprehensions in 2019.
rationales.general:
1. Compare the two years. Background: in 2000, single adults from Mexico dominated the flow.
2. Background: in 2019, families were 473,682 of 851,508 apprehensions, more than half.
3. Background: most of those families came from El Salvador, Guatemala, and Honduras, not Mexico.
4. The rebound was a change in who arrived, not just in how many arrived.
Remember: when a total jumps, ask whether the people behind it changed too.
